_note: Research pass of November 2026: Europe, the Middle East and Oceania, the three regions with the fewest listings. Facts were checked against the organisers' own pages as returned by web search; the pages themselves could not be opened in that session, so no entry here is rated above medium confidence.

commissions.name: 1% artistique
commissions.org: Ministère de la Culture, with the State and local authorities as commissioners
commissions.summary: France's percent-for-art obligation, in force since 1951. One per cent of the cost of building, extending or renovating most public buildings of the State and of local authorities must go to commissioning or buying original work from living artists, conceived for that building. The scope and the procurement rules are set by Decree 2002-677 of 29 April 2002.
commissions.budgetNote: One per cent of the construction cost of the building concerned, so the budget is different for every project. No national fee scale for artists is published.
commissions.cycleNote: Not a single annual round. Each new project is, with limited exceptions, put out as a call for applications to artists, and an artistic committee for the project sets the brief and gives its opinion on the proposals. The Ministry of Culture lists the calls that are open on its site, so that page is the one to watch.

commissions.name: Kunst am Bau (federal buildings)
commissions.org: Federal Ministry for Housing, Urban Development and Building (BMWSB)
commissions.summary: The German federal government's art-in-architecture programme, which commissions work for federal buildings. Since July 2024 it has run under a binding ministerial decree that replaced the earlier guideline, and spending on art should not exceed 1.5 per cent of a building's construction costs.
commissions.budgetNote: Up to 1.5 per cent of the building's construction costs, counted as cost groups 300 and 400 under DIN 276. The actual sum is set project by project.
commissions.cycleNote: Project by project, through art competitions run under the same rules as architecture competitions. Some are open competitions that any professional artist can enter and others are by invitation; one large federal project ran three open and four invited competitions. Each competition's own brief says who may enter.

commissions.name: Per Cent for Art Scheme
commissions.org: Government of Ireland, through each department, agency or local authority that builds
commissions.summary: A government scheme, open to every capital construction project across all departments since 1997, that lets part of a project's budget be spent on a new art commission. It is paid for from within the building project's own budget and run under national guidelines that give commissioners one common approach.
commissions.budgetNote: Spending is set by published investment bands, each with a maximum for projects of that size; the current bands and limits took effect on 1 January 2020. Check the guidelines for the figure that applies to a given project.
commissions.cycleNote: Calls appear as building projects reach the right stage, not on a fixed date. Depending on the project, artists are chosen by open call, by limited competition or by another route, and some local authorities name nationally advertised open competition as their main method. A national committee has been reviewing the scheme and its guidelines since 2022, so terms may change.

commissions.name: Legge 717/1949 — the "two per cent law"
commissions.org: Ministry of Culture, Directorate-General for Contemporary Creativity, with each public body that builds
commissions.summary: An Italian law of 1949 that requires public administrations building or substantially altering public buildings to set aside part of the cost for works of art made for them. Some building types are excluded, among them industrial buildings and social housing. The Ministry of Culture runs a dedicated portal for the law and, under a 2025 circular, oversees how the works are delivered.
commissions.budgetNote: The law is known for its two per cent figure. Later amendments made the share vary with the size of the project, and the thresholds now in force could not be confirmed, so read the notice for each competition.
commissions.cycleNote: Artists are chosen through competitions announced project by project by the body that is building, under ministerial guidelines last updated in 2017. There is no single annual round; the ministry's portal for the law is the place to look.

commissions.name: Commissioning of Artworks Act (the "percentage act")
commissions.org: Estonian Ministry of Culture, with juries appointed by the Estonian Artists' Association
commissions.summary: Estonia's percent-for-art law, in force since 2011. When a public building is built or renovated, about one per cent of the construction cost goes to commissioning art for it. Works are chosen through design competitions, and the Estonian Artists' Association appoints jury members for them.
commissions.budgetNote: Up to about one per cent of the building's construction cost. A ceiling per commission has been reported in the press but could not be confirmed from an official source.
commissions.cycleNote: Competitions are announced one building at a time through the year. The Estonian Artists' Association publishes current art procurements on its site.

commissions.name: Art Commission (Kunstopdracht)
commissions.org: Mondriaan Fund
commissions.summary: A grant from the Dutch public fund for visual art that helps pay for a newly commissioned work shown publicly in the Netherlands or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom. It is the commissioner, not the artist, who applies: anyone who does not intend to sell the work can commission a professional visual artist with it.
commissions.budgetNote: Set per application on the advice of a committee. Under the fund's 2021–2024 rules the grant covered up to half the costs of a concrete commission, or up to 70 per cent of a development phase to a maximum of €15,000, and the artist's fee could be part of the budget. Check the current page for today's figures.
commissions.cycleNote: Applications come from the commissioner, so an artist needs a client willing to apply. Under the 2021–2024 rules the commissioned artist had to have worked professionally for at least a year and be registered with the Dutch Chamber of Commerce.

commissions.name: KÖR — Public Art Vienna
commissions.org: KÖR Kunst im öffentlichen Raum Wien GmbH
commissions.summary: The City of Vienna's body for art in public space, which funds and realises permanent and temporary projects across the city. Its open calls have invited not only artists but also architects, urban and landscape designers and local groups to propose projects for a named site or theme.
commissions.budgetNote: Set call by call. No standing rate appears in the material checked.
commissions.cycleNote: Themed and site-specific open calls are published from time to time on KÖR's own site, and a call for permanent and temporary work was listed for 2026. Dates move every year, so check the current call.

commissions.name: Percent for Art principle
commissions.org: Arts Promotion Centre Finland (Taike), with municipalities and other builders
commissions.summary: A principle, not a law, under which at least one per cent of a construction budget is spent on art. It is applied to new buildings, renovations and environmental construction alike, and how it works differs from one city to the next; in Helsinki most public art is paid for this way.
commissions.budgetNote: About one per cent of the construction cost of the project concerned. Taike has also awarded subsidies to projects that apply the principle, published with its other grants.
commissions.cycleNote: No single national call. Each city or builder decides how to choose artists. Taike's public art team advises on commissioning, and its grants pages carry any open subsidy calls.

commissions.name: One Percent Rule
commissions.org: Public Art Agency Sweden (Statens konstråd), with regions and municipalities
commissions.summary: Sweden's rule that at least one per cent of the cost of a building project should go to public art, introduced by a government bill in 1937 that also founded Public Art Agency Sweden. There has never been one fixed model for it, so the state, regions and municipalities apply it in their own ways; by the agency's count 41 per cent of municipalities and 55 per cent of regions use it.
commissions.budgetNote: At least one per cent of the total building cost where the rule is applied. How the sum is calculated varies between commissioners.
commissions.cycleNote: Commissions are tied to individual building projects, not to a calendar. How artists are chosen was not set out in the agency pages checked and differs between the state agency, regions and municipalities, so ask the commissioner of the project you are interested in.

commissions.name: Public art commissions of the Danish Arts Foundation
commissions.org: Danish Arts Foundation (Statens Kunstfond)
commissions.summary: The Danish state's arts foundation commissions art for public places together with state, regional and municipal institutions, which apply to work with it. Its committees choose the artists, as they did for the five artists given the stations of Copenhagen's Sydhavn metro line, with artistic quality as the overriding test.
commissions.budgetNote: Set per project. Smaller decoration tasks, under DKK 250,000, can be decided by the client without going to the Foundation.
commissions.cycleNote: Mostly by the Foundation's own selection, not by application. It can also run open calls for sketch proposals and idea competitions, but does so on a smaller scale. It is municipalities, not artists, that apply for its support for art in public space.

commissions.name: Ithra Art Prize
commissions.org: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture (Ithra)
commissions.summary: A prize awarded for a proposed artwork by Ithra, the cultural centre in Dhahran; the winning work enters Ithra's permanent collection. The seventh edition was open to individual artists and collectives aged 18 or over who are of Arab heritage or live in one of the 22 Arab countries.
commissions.budgetNote: US$100,000 to the winner in the seventh edition, with production grants for five finalists to show their work. Earlier editions added a separate production budget. There is no fee to enter.
commissions.cycleNote: An open call for each edition; the seventh opened in July 2025 and named its winner the following spring. Terms change between editions, including whether the work must be entirely new, so read the current conditions.

commissions.name: Art Here and the Richard Mille Art Prize
commissions.org: Louvre Abu Dhabi, with Richard Mille
commissions.summary: An annual exhibition and prize at Louvre Abu Dhabi. Artists answer a call for proposals for large sculptures and installations; those shortlisted have their works commissioned and shown in the exhibition, and one receives the prize.
commissions.budgetNote: A grand prize of US$60,000 in the 2026 edition, up from US$50,000 when the prize began in 2021. Shortlisted works are commissioned for the exhibition.
commissions.cycleNote: One call for proposals a year, closing in late spring in 2026, with the exhibition opening in the autumn. Who may apply changes with every edition: the 2026 call was open to nationals and residents of the Gulf Cooperation Council countries and to Indian nationals, while the 2025 edition paired the Gulf with Japan.

commissions.name: Qatar Museums public art open calls
commissions.org: Qatar Museums
commissions.summary: Qatar Museums runs several recurring open calls that commission public art: JedariArt for murals and street art, the 5/6 Initiative for a permanent work, an annual intervention, a student strand and, since 2024, a temporary public art call for artists early in their careers. Successful applicants are commissioned to carry out their proposal.
commissions.budgetNote: Selected artists receive a commission contract. Amounts are not given in the notices checked.
commissions.cycleNote: Each strand has its own call and its own rule on who may enter. JedariArt has been limited to artists living in Qatar with a valid residence permit, while the 5/6 Initiative was open to residents of all Gulf Cooperation Council countries in 2023. The notices found date from 2020 to 2024, so confirm the current round on the Qatar Museums site.

commissions.name: Dubai Public Art
commissions.org: Dubai Culture and Arts Authority, with partners including the Roads and Transport Authority and Art Jameel
commissions.summary: The public art programme of Dubai's culture authority, which commissions permanent works for the city through a run of open calls. Recent calls have covered more than forty road tunnels, the city's main roundabouts and a playscape beside the Jameel Arts Centre.
commissions.budgetNote: Set per commission. No standing budget appears in the announcements checked.
commissions.cycleNote: Calls are announced one site at a time, typically with a jury that shortlists a few proposals for development. They have been open to artists, designers and architects based in the United Arab Emirates, and some to Emirati practitioners only. The tunnels call ran in May and June 2026.

commissions.name: The Christo and Jeanne-Claude Award
commissions.org: NYU Abu Dhabi, with the Abu Dhabi Music and Arts Foundation (ADMAF)
commissions.summary: An annual award that pays for one new work proposed by an artist based in the United Arab Emirates, aimed above all at students and recent graduates. The finished work is shown at NYU Abu Dhabi and then at other venues.
commissions.budgetNote: US$10,000 to develop the proposed work over about six months. Applicants submit their own budget with the proposal.
commissions.cycleNote: An open call each year for artists based in the UAE. For the 2026 edition submissions opened in October and closed at the end of January, with the work shown the following November.

commissions.name: Noor Riyadh
commissions.org: Riyadh Art, Royal Commission for Riyadh City
commissions.summary: An annual festival of light and art across Riyadh, presented by Riyadh Art, which also runs Tuwaiq Sculpture. The 2025 edition showed 60 works by 59 artists of 24 nationalities, more than 35 of them new commissions, chosen by a curatorial team.
commissions.budgetNote: New works are commissioned and produced by the festival. Fees and budgets are not published.
commissions.cycleNote: Curated: artists are selected by each edition's curators and announced as a line-up. No open call for the festival was found, unlike Tuwaiq Sculpture, which Riyadh Art does open to applications.

commissions.name: Desert X AlUla
commissions.org: Royal Commission for AlUla, with Desert X
commissions.summary: A recurring exhibition of site-responsive works commissioned for the desert landscape around AlUla. The fourth edition ran in early 2026 with eleven artists under the title Space Without Measure, curated by Wejdan Reda and Zoé Whitley.
commissions.budgetNote: Works are commissioned for the exhibition. Fees and production budgets are not published.
commissions.cycleNote: By curatorial selection. Artists visit AlUla and make proposals, and the curators choose from those; past curators have described balancing Saudi, regional and international artists. There is no open call.

commissions.name: Percent for Art Scheme (Western Australia)
commissions.org: Government of Western Australia, Department of Finance
commissions.summary: Western Australia's scheme for commissioning art with state building projects, usually with one per cent of the construction cost. Under the 2025 guidelines it applies to new buildings and major additions with an estimated construction cost above A$2 million.
commissions.budgetNote: Usually one per cent of the project's construction cost. Each commission's budget is stated in its brief.
commissions.cycleNote: Project by project. Calls for artists are published as expressions of interest on the state's Tenders WA site, where you need to register to read them, and each brief sets out the stages and selection criteria. Some projects engage Aboriginal artists directly instead of through an open call.

commissions.name: Tasmanian Government Art Site Scheme
commissions.org: Arts Tasmania
commissions.summary: Tasmania's public art scheme, which commissions work for new and renovated state government buildings; recent calls were for schools, a sports arena and emergency services buildings. It rests on the principle that two per cent of the building estimate goes to art.
commissions.budgetNote: Two per cent of the pre-tender estimate for state building projects above A$250,000, as the government has described the scheme. Shortlisted artists have been paid a fee to develop a concept, A$1,000 in one recent call.
commissions.cycleNote: Calls open one building at a time as expressions of interest; a committee shortlists up to about six artists, who then prepare a fuller concept. Only Tasmanian artists can apply. Current calls are on Arts Tasmania's public art page.

commissions.name: The Collin Post 4 Plinths Project
commissions.org: Wellington Sculpture Trust
commissions.summary: A temporary sculpture commission for the four concrete plinths on the forecourt of Te Papa, the national museum, renewed every two years. The artist keeps the work when it comes down.
commissions.budgetNote: The Trust has announced NZ$100,000 for the award with installation planned for 2028, double the NZ$50,000 of the round before. Earlier briefs charged a small fee per proposal.
commissions.cycleNote: A call for proposals every two years, open to New Zealand and international artists. Check the Trust's current brief for the closing date and conditions.

commissions.name: Sculpture by the Sea, Bondi
commissions.org: Sculpture by the Sea
commissions.summary: An outdoor sculpture exhibition on the Bondi coast, held each spring. Sculpture of any type, size and material can be submitted, by artists at any stage of their career.
commissions.budgetNote: Exhibiting is not paid, and the organisers do not cover freight, airfares, accommodation or fabrication. Awards and subsidies offset this for some artists and change every year; in 2024 the main acquisitive award was A$70,000 and one artist subsidy was A$5,000.
commissions.cycleNote: Open submissions once a year for Australian and international artists; the 2026 round closed in April for an exhibition in October and November.

commissions.name: Test Sites
commissions.org: City of Melbourne
commissions.summary: A development programme from the City of Melbourne that backs up to five artists a year to work up and try out a new idea for public art. It is for ideas at an early stage, not for producing a finished or previously shown project, and comes with workshops and a mentor.
commissions.budgetNote: Between A$10,000 and A$20,000 towards costs for each selected artist in the 2025 and 2026 rounds.
commissions.cycleNote: An open expression of interest once a year; the 2026 round closed in March. Applicants must be based in Victoria, and artists in any art form can apply.

commissions.name: SCAPE Public Art
commissions.org: SCAPE Public Art
commissions.summary: A yearly season of contemporary art in the public spaces of Christchurch. A managing curator sets the theme and chooses the artists for the main season; six were invited for 2025.
commissions.budgetNote: Works for the season are commissioned and produced by SCAPE. Budgets are not published.
commissions.cycleNote: The main season is by invitation. Alongside it SCAPE has run Re:ACTIVATE, an open call for emerging artists judged by a local panel, and a competition for school-age entrants. No open call for the current year was found, so check the SCAPE site.

residencies.name: Solitude Fellowship
residencies.duration: Six or nine months for individuals; six months for collectives
residencies.funding: Funded: a monthly fellowship of €1,300 in the 2026–2028 cycle (€1,200 in the cycle before), a furnished live-in studio and a one-off travel allowance for arrival and departure.
residencies.disciplines: Artists, researchers and cultural practitioners across disciplines, with a separate strand for the sciences
residencies.summary: Akademie Schloss Solitude awards between 50 and 60 international residencies every two years. Fellows are expected to live in Stuttgart for the length of the fellowship.
residencies.applicationNote: An open call every two years in three stages, beginning with a short online application; the call for 2026–2028 opened in autumn 2025. Former fellows cannot reapply and each person may submit one application per call. Listings disagree on the experience or degree required, so read the academy's own call.

residencies.name: Jan van Eyck Academie
residencies.duration: About eleven months, from mid-January to mid-December
residencies.funding: Part funded: a monthly stipend and a one-off material budget of €2,000 are provided, and recent listings also show a one-off programme fee of €2,750 and a €65 application fee. Stipend figures differ between listings and years, and rent may be deducted, so confirm the current terms.
residencies.disciplines: Artists, designers, architects, curators, writers and other researchers; individuals, duos and collectives
residencies.summary: A post-academic institute offering around thirty places a year, built around labs and workshops, not a taught course. Participants are expected to settle in Maastricht for the residency.
residencies.applicationNote: One open call a year in the autumn for a residency starting more than a year later; the call for 2027 ran from October to December 2025 with results the following May. Earlier calls excluded people who had held a place at another Dutch post-academic institute.

residencies.name: HIAP — Helsinki International Artist Programme
residencies.duration: Three months for the international open call
residencies.funding: Varies by call. The international programme provides a place to live and work on Suomenlinna island or at the Cable Factory; some partner-funded places carry a grant, and the curators' residency lists a €1,200 working grant and a travel allowance. Confirm what the call you apply to covers.
residencies.disciplines: Artists and other art practitioners, with a separate strand for curators
residencies.summary: An international residency centre on the island of Suomenlinna and at the Cable Factory in Helsinki. It grants about eight three-month residencies from its international open call, alongside separate programmes for artists based in Finland.
residencies.applicationNote: An annual international open call for artists who are not based in Finland; the call for 2026 closed in July 2025. Finland-based artists apply to different calls, and several places are filled through funders in other countries.

residencies.name: Nordic Artists' Centre Dale (NKD)
residencies.funding: Funded: a monthly grant of NOK 11,000 and travel costs up to NOK 5,000 in the call for 2027, with a private house and a 50 m² north-lit studio for each resident.
residencies.summary: Five houses and five studios in western Norway, each resident with a house and studio of their own. Residents give a talk and take part in an open studio day.
residencies.applicationNote: One open call a year, about a year ahead of the residency; the call for 2026 closed in March 2025. Full-time students cannot apply, and applicants from outside the Nordic region are expected to work in English.

residencies.name: WIELS Residency Programme
residencies.duration: Three to six months; most sessions are six months
residencies.funding: Depends on the route. Artists based in Belgium get a studio but no accommodation. International residents come with a partner funder that usually covers a 40 m² studio, accommodation, travel and a monthly stipend, which ranged from about €850 to €1,300 in recent partner calls.
residencies.summary: Up to twenty artists a year work in studios inside the WIELS contemporary art centre. It is two programmes in one: a call for artists in Belgium, and a set of country-by-country places funded by partners abroad.
residencies.applicationNote: Artists who are Belgian, or who have worked in Belgium for at least three years, apply through a call published each May for two six-month sessions a year. Everyone else applies through the funder for their own country, each with its own eligibility rules and timetable, so there is no general international call.

residencies.name: Gasworks Residencies
residencies.funding: Fully funded in the calls checked: return flights, a private studio with round-the-clock access, a room in a house shared with the other residents, living costs and materials.
residencies.disciplines: Visual arts, for artists early in their careers
residencies.summary: Gasworks hosts up to twenty international artists a year in studios at its building in London. Each place is paid for by a partner and reserved for artists based in one country or region.
residencies.applicationNote: Open calls are published one country or region at a time through the year on the Gasworks opportunities page; recent calls covered Italy, Brazil, Aotearoa New Zealand and several regions of Africa. Students cannot apply, and a shortlist is interviewed online.

residencies.name: MeetFactory Artist-in-Residence
residencies.duration: Varies by call; stays of about two months are common
residencies.funding: Depends on the call and its partner. One 2025 call paid €1,000 a month plus production costs up to €3,000; an earlier open call for foreign artists listed a monthly allowance of CZK 17,000. Check the call you apply to.
residencies.disciplines: Visual arts, with some calls in other fields
residencies.summary: An international centre for contemporary art in Prague with studios for visiting artists. Its residencies run as a series of separate calls, many with partner institutions abroad.
residencies.applicationNote: No single annual deadline. Calls are posted on MeetFactory's programme page through the year, some open to artists anywhere and others to artists from a partner country or already living in Prague.

residencies.name: Rupert Residency Programme
residencies.duration: One to three months, proposed by the applicant
residencies.funding: Not fully funded as standard. Residents get a furnished studio of about 52 m² with a mezzanine; Rupert issues acceptance letters and helps residents apply for outside grants to cover the residency fee, travel and living costs. Older calls promised that at least half the places would be grant-funded, which could not be confirmed for recent ones.
residencies.disciplines: Artists, writers, curators, researchers and academics
residencies.summary: An independent centre for art, residencies and education in Vilnius. Applicants say whether their project is research or production, and how long they want to stay.
residencies.applicationNote: An open call, with an application fee of about €20 in the most recent listing found. Rupert also takes part in fully funded joint residencies with partners, which have their own calls.

residencies.name: IASPIS — the Swedish Arts Grants Committee's international programme
residencies.funding: Described in listings as fully funded. The exact provision could not be confirmed from the committee's own pages.
residencies.summary: The international programme of the Swedish Arts Grants Committee, with residencies in Stockholm, Gothenburg, Malmö and Umeå. It brings international practitioners to Sweden and sends artists based in Sweden abroad.
residencies.applicationNote: The route depends on the residency. Some places are filled by open call; for others, such as Malmö, international artists are proposed by local institutions and then invited. Exchange places abroad are generally reserved for artists who live or work in Sweden. Check the current call before assuming you can apply directly.

residencies.name: Culture Moves Europe — Individual Mobility
residencies.duration: Short stays, within the number of days set in each call
residencies.funding: A grant, not a hosted residency: in the 2025–2026 call a travel allowance of €400 for journeys under 5,000 km and a daily allowance of €85.
residencies.summary: The European Union's mobility scheme for artists, paid for by Creative Europe. It funds a project carried out with a partner in another participating country, so it is one way to pay for a stay abroad that has no funding of its own.
residencies.applicationNote: Open to people aged 18 or over who legally reside in a Creative Europe country, alone or in groups of up to five. The project needs an international partner and cannot already have taken place. Calls stay open for several months with cut-off dates along the way, and in the current period each person can receive one grant.

residencies.name: Fire Station: Artist in Residence
residencies.duration: Nine months, from September to June
residencies.funding: A studio in the Fire Station building for the full term. A monthly stipend was reported in the programme's early years, but the current amount could not be confirmed.
residencies.summary: Qatar Museums' residency for artists living and working in Qatar, in the Fire Station building in Doha. Each resident is given a studio on one of its five floors.
residencies.applicationNote: An annual open call, announced at the start of each calendar year and judged by a panel of five to seven. The detailed eligibility rules for the current year were not available, so check the call.

residencies.name: Tashkeel — Critical Practice Programme
residencies.funding: Studio space and tailored support for the length of the programme. No stipend is mentioned in the calls checked.
residencies.summary: A year of studio support from Tashkeel, an art and design centre in Dubai, with a plan built around each artist. What residents make feeds into Tashkeel's exhibition programme.
residencies.applicationNote: An open call for visual arts practitioners living and working in the UAE, issued in the autumn in past years. Tashkeel runs other residencies and a design programme with their own calls.

residencies.name: Masaha Residency
residencies.funding: A private studio, a production budget and a public showcase at the end, according to the institute. Listings add accommodation for artists from outside Riyadh, and one mentions flights and visa support for international residents, which should be confirmed.
residencies.disciplines: Visual arts in all media, for artists working full time
residencies.summary: The Misk Art Institute's residency in Riyadh, run in numbered cycles. The eleventh ran from May to July 2026.
residencies.applicationNote: An open call for each cycle. Recent cycles were open to international as well as Saudi artists with at least three years of professional experience, and residents must commit full time for the three months.

residencies.name: Darat al Funun — The Lab, Summer Academy and fellowship
residencies.funding: Differs by route. The dissertation fellowship provides housing and a place to work; for projects at The Lab the foundation does not pay international applicants' travel or insurance, though it may offer one of its residency flats.
residencies.disciplines: Visual arts, film, design, architecture, performance, curating and research
residencies.summary: The Khalid Shoman Foundation's home for the arts in Amman. It has no single residency; instead it opens several calls a year, each for a different kind of practitioner.
residencies.applicationNote: Three routes were found. Projects at The Lab are open to artists, filmmakers, designers, architects, performers and curators. The Summer Academy is for emerging artists based in Jordan and Palestine. A dissertation fellowship takes one or two researchers a cycle. Each has its own deadline.

residencies.name: Ashkal Alwan — Home Workspace Program
residencies.duration: About ten months in earlier editions; the fifteenth edition ran from January to July 2026
residencies.funding: Tuition was free for selected fellows in the calls found, which are several years old. Those calls do not show living costs being covered; confirm the current terms.
residencies.disciplines: Contemporary art practice in all forms
residencies.summary: A non-degree study programme run by Ashkal Alwan in Beirut, built from workshops and one-to-one sessions with mentors. It takes a small group of fellows for each edition.
residencies.applicationNote: By open call, with shortlisted applicants interviewed. Earlier calls welcomed applicants from Lebanon, the Arab region and elsewhere, asked for working Arabic or English, and admitted between ten and eighteen fellows. The terms of the next call were not available.

residencies.name: Gertrude Studio Program
residencies.funding: Subsidised, not free: sixteen studios are let well below market rate, at A$280 a month in the 2023 call with a refundable bond. One further studio a year is fully subsidised for a First Nations artist.
residencies.summary: Sixteen studios at Gertrude Contemporary in Preston South, each held for two years. Artists of any generation can apply.
residencies.applicationNote: An open call each year, assessed by a committee of Gertrude staff, a current and a former studio artist and an outside curator. Artists who have held a Gertrude studio before, or who will be studying during the two years, cannot apply.

residencies.name: Artspace Studio Program
residencies.duration: One or two years; Artspace is moving towards two-year residencies
residencies.funding: Rent-free: ten studios of about 45 m² with a kitchenette, a desk and round-the-clock access. No stipend is mentioned.
residencies.summary: Free studios at Artspace, offered rent-free since 2015 and increased from seven to ten when the building was redeveloped in 2023. Residents take part in open studios and meet visiting curators through Artspace.
residencies.applicationNote: One open call a year; applications outside that window are not considered. The 2025 intake offered five one-year and five two-year places. The eligibility rules were not available, so read the guidelines linked from the studio page.

residencies.name: Walyalup Fremantle Arts Centre — Studios and Residencies
residencies.funding: Studios in the centre's Studios Program carry no rent, though artists pay their own production costs. Residencies add an apartment in Fremantle, and exchange places with partners overseas have come with flights and a bursary.
residencies.summary: Studios and a residency apartment at the arts centre in Fremantle, open to local, Australian and international artists. It also runs exchanges with partner institutions, among them Incheon Art Platform in South Korea.
residencies.applicationNote: By application when a call is open; the centre's page showed applications closed when checked. Exchange places can be limited to artists who live and work in Western Australia.

residencies.name: Te Whare Hēra — Wellington International Artist Residency
residencies.duration: About two months in its first year
residencies.funding: When it launched in 2014 the residency covered travel, accommodation, an honorarium and a materials allowance. The current package could not be confirmed.
residencies.summary: A residency for artists from overseas, run by Massey University's College of Creative Arts with Wellington City Council. The college has said it has tended to host established artists and would like to support emerging ones as well.
residencies.applicationNote: By invitation. When the programme began there was no proposal or application process, and no open call was found since.
